title: solstice-account-playbook-wip
content:
Quick notes / working playbook for Solstice Retail (initial outbound + call plan)

Account snapshot:
- Company: Solstice Retail (mid-market, omnichannel apparel retailer, ~220 stores North America + ecommerce).
- Why we care: they have in-app conversational search and in-store POS assistants in pilot. High token volume but strict latency needs for store interactions.
- Key business driver: reduce cart abandonment on mobile + improve in-store associate TLDRs (30–60s responses with product recs).
- Estimated monthly usage (ops guess): 150M–300M tokens depending on pilot success (chat + embeddings for search).

Primary contacts (research notes):
- Priya Shah – Head of Digital Product (LinkedIn: priya-shah-solstice). owns mobile/apps. Likely economic buyer for pilot.
- Tom Rivera – Director, Store Ops. cares about latency and offline fallback.
- Lisa Nguyen – Engineering manager, ML infra. will ask about private deployment + KMS.

Key pain points (from job posts & call hints):
- Current provider cost is unpredictable on peak sale days.
- Latency spikes during peak (flash promotions) cause poor in-store experience.
- Data sensitivity for POS queries + PII concerns (want control over logs).

Redwood hooks tailored to Solstice:
- Predictable cost via Dedicated capacity (monthly commits) to tame surge pricing.
- Private deployment / VPC option to satisfy POS data controls and KMS integration.
- Smart routing: route in-store low-latency requests to nearest region or dedicated pool to hit store SLOs.
- Prefix/KV caching for product SKUs & catalog descriptions to reduce token spend for repeated queries.
- Console: token-level cost + per-route latency dashboards to show CFO/ops clear ROI.

Technical pre-emptive answers (expected Lisa questions):
- Integration: REST + SDKs, webhook for store events; simple sidecar for local inference in air-gapped retail edge (we have private deployment options).
- Authentication/KMS: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. Audit logs for queries.
- Quantization & perf: can recommend 8-bit quantized variants to lower GPU cost on Dedicated.

Pricing frame to use (quick):
- Pilot: Dedicated small pool estimate: $6k–$12k/month (elastic burst + 99th% latency SLA).
- Hosted API alternative: usage-based (predictable only with careful rate & cache configs) -> risk of runaway during promos.
- Ask for current monthly spend with existing provider (baseline).

Outbound email drafts (A/B test):
- Subject A: Quick idea to stabilize Solstice in-store AI latency
  Hi Priya —
  Quick intro: I’m Maya at Redwood Inference. We help retailers run conversational search and in-store assistants with predictable latency and cost.
  Saw Solstice’s pilot for in-store POS assistants — you mentioned latency spikes on promos in the job listing (link). We helped another mid-market chain cut 95th percentile latency by 40% using a small dedicated pool + prefix caching.
  Curious if you’d be open to a 20-minute call next week to compare notes and share a short cost/latency model for your pilot?
  —Maya

- Subject B: Protect promo-day performance for Solstice (20 min)
  Hi Priya —
  Two quick things: 1) predictable Dedicated pools to avoid promo-day price spikes; 2) private deployment/KMS options for POS data.
  If you’re running promos next quarter, a quick model we run takes ~15 minutes to produce a cost/latency forecast. Free if useful.
  Cheers, Maya

Voicemail / cold call opener (30s):
- Hi Priya, this is Maya Chen at Redwood. Saw Solstice’s in-store AI pilot — we’ve helped retailers keep their in-store assistants fast on promo days while cutting monthly inference costs. I’d love 15 minutes to show a before/after latency/cost snapshot. I’ll follow up by email — thanks!

Suggested call agenda (20 min):
- 3 min quick intros & success metrics they care about (cart conversion, store NPS).
- 5 min current architecture + pain points (where latency happens).
- 7 min what Redwood can do: Dedicated pool sketch, private deploy options, caching, and a quick cost model.
- 3–5 min next steps (pilot scope + stakeholders).

Objections + short counters (bullet cheatsheet):
- "We already have a vendor" -> Great — ask what they can’t do (latency on promos? private deploy?). Offer a non-disruptive proof where we run parallel routing for a week.
- "We can’t commit to dedicated spend" -> Offer hosted pilot with strict burst caps + caching + an estimate of when Dedicated is cost-effective (show math).
- "Security/compliance concerns" -> Private deployment + customer KMS + audit logs. Offer SSO + SOC docs (link in Confluence).
- "Engineering bandwidth" -> Provide integration template (sidecar + SDK) and offer solutions engineering support for the pilot kickoff (2–3 sprints estimate).

Quick technical checklist to bring to discovery (for Lisa):
- how many concurrent store sessions at peak?
- average sequence length (chat) and embeddings volume per day
- catalog size and update cadence (affects cache invalidation)
- POS connectivity constraints (offline scenarios)
- security: PCI scope and whether SSO/KMS required

Pilot proposal (sketch):
- 6-week pilot focused on 30 stores + mobile users in two regions.
- deliverables: latency & cost baseline, dedicated pool config, caching rules, dashboard access, runbook for failover.
- success criteria: 95th percentile latency under 250ms for in-store prompts; 20% reduction in token cost per convo.

Next steps / Ask:
- Send intro email + calendar options -> get 15–20m with Priya + Lisa.
- Ask for baseline metrics (current provider monthly spend, latency p50/p95, token counts) ahead of call.
- Internal: loop Arjun for solutions scoping and EM from infra for notes.

Notes to self / TODOs: 
- Prep two one-pagers: 1) Dedicated pilot cost model template; 2) Private deploy checklist for retail.
- Pull a short case study for a similar retailer (ask CS for redacted numbers).
- Draft a one-slide latency vs cost graph to attach to email.
- Check Confluence for SOC 2 and PCI artifacts to reference.

Random scratch thoughts (untidy):
- If they have store edge boxes, run a quick POC of a small inference container at edge (could sell as premium).
- Consider offering a "promo mode" config: auto-prioritize critical routes to dedicated pool during sales. Could be a quick productized feature ask.
- Keep price talk simple in first outreach — emphasize predictability + SLA.

End of doc.
